newsitem.title: SPAIN: Car bomb kills one, injures seven in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Car bomb kills one, injures seven in Spain.

text.p: One person was killed and seven were injured in a car bomb explosion close to a military base in the southern Spanish city of Granada on Monday, police said.
The Interior Ministry said the explosion was likely to have been a guerrilla attack by Basque separatist group ETA.

"Everthing is very confused at the moment as it usually is after a terrorist attack but sadly we can confirm there is one person dead," State Secretary for the Interior Ricardo Marti told local radio.
Police said the blast occurred on a road leading to a military base, about two km (one mile) from the city centre, at around 0615 GMT.
The victim was a hairdresser travelling in a military van to Granada's Armilla military airbase, the interior ministry said. Of the seven injured, police said three had been seriously hurt.
Police said the explosion had been huge, breaking windows in a wide area and seriously damaging a nearby building up to the fourth floor.
ETA has frequently targeted security forces and police in its 29-year fight for an independent Basque state, in which it has killed some 800 people.
Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said the attack was proof the government should not enter into talks with ETA.
"It's important to understand that ETA's sole aim is to make the population feel permanently threatened," Oreja told state radio.

In January a Spanish army officer was shot and killed in Madrid in what the government branded an ETA assassination. The car supposedly used by the attackers was blown up nearby injuring a members of the Royal Guard who was passing by.
Over the weekend, dozens of people were injured and property was damaged in protests and demonstrations in the northern Basque region after an alleged ETA prisoner was found hanged in his cell.
An autopsy report revealed that the prisoner had been depressed for several weeks and had killed himself, but hundreds of Basques took to the streets claiming it was murder.
They carried banners and chanted slogans: "The people will not forgive" and "Assassins, you have killed another prisoner".
